title: 13th Sitting of first Session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened at 10:34 and the Speaker declined an urgent question from the Keyodhoo member because it did not meet the Rules of Procedure. The government's bill to amend the Tourism Act (Law 99/2), sponsored by Thimarafushi member Ahmed Riyaz, had its first reading and then began its preliminary debate. Members argued over lease terms and discounts, the role of island councils in allocating tourism land, the proposed Tourism Trust Fund, and the state of the economy, with several heated points of order that the Speaker did not accept. The debate did not finish; the Speaker said he would let all members who wished to speak do so before a vote and adjourned at 12:01 until the next sitting on Wednesday 12 March 2025.

items.title: Praises and prayers; opening of the sitting
Attendance of members
items.outcome: 42 present, 5 on leave, 1 on official travel (figures partly garbled in source)

items.title: Announcements from the chair (urgent question from Keyodhoo member Mohamed Niushad, Rule 192)
items.outcome: Speaker said the conditions in Rule 197 (k) and (d) were not met, so the question would not be presented

items.title: Bill to amend the Tourism Act, Law 99/2 (government bill, sponsored by Thimarafushi member Ahmed Riyaz)
Preliminary debate on the bill to amend the Tourism Act, Law 99/2
items.outcome: debated; not concluded; many members still wished to speak and the sitting was adjourned, to continue on 12 March 2025

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Raised points of order on the lease-payment figures quoted and on remarks he considered off the topic of the bill.
Backed the bill, saying it gives councils authority over tourism land in their area and that the PNC parliamentary group supports government bills.
Rejected claims that the government will print money and called on members to avoid personal accusations during Ramadan.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Raised a point of order that Inguraidhoo's member was straying from the bill, and later objected to being addressed by name.
Regretted that an urgent question on Addu power cuts was blocked the previous day, and criticised spending of tourism income and contracts to state companies.
Said he would vote for the bill if it helps development, but asked the government for a long-term policy and action on waste.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Questioned the lease-extension and discount payment terms, saying the changes were drawn up without a clear long-term plan.
Criticised provisions forcing lease changes when a resort closes for repairs and letting the state reclaim a resort not reopened in time.
Asked for investor-friendly laws and a clearer hotel definition; also raised a point of order that opponents were speaking off the bill.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Raised a point of order denying that MDP members protested in a way that disturbed Ramadan prayers.
Opposed the bill, saying amendments come without a clear policy and drain council powers toward the President.
Argued the law already bars tourist services on council land, and linked MVR 14 billion in money printing to rising prices.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Fully supported the bill, saying governments routinely amend tourism law to benefit citizens and the bill does not take power from councils.
Disputed claims that the government would print money and said Parliament should debate the bill as written.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Supported the bill, saying tourism is the country's main income source and councils deciding tourism land fits the infrastructure plan.
Said the bill is thorough and that committee stage can add expert advice, and blamed past MDP governments for harming tourism.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Raised a point of order saying current practice, not this bill, already gives the President power over which islands and reefs are allocated.
Supported the bill, saying laws are amended as the economy changes and the bill mostly writes existing practice into law.

speakers.name: Ahmed Riyaz
positions: Introduced the bill, saying it amends cross-subsidy and lease-extension rules for tourist resorts and sets up a Tourism Trust Fund to grow tourism income.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Opposed the bill, saying a third amendment in months shows no long-term policy and moves land powers from councils to the President.
Warned that sudden changes hurt investor confidence and cited power cuts affecting guesthouses in Addu City.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Rejected claims that the economy is collapsing, citing growth in reserves and tourist arrivals, and said the amendments help investors.
Said street protests could discourage tourists and criticised earlier MDP-led governments' record on tourism.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Supported the bill, saying it empowers councils to decide tourism land and gives investors more certainty.
Denied that resorts would be taken back unfairly and said the changes follow the President's manifesto.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the amendments, saying land allocation rules and the Tourism Trust Fund matter, but cross-subsidy land should be reclaimed if work is not done.
Called on the government to investigate causes of the debt and economic strain.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Questioned the government's vision for tourism, given three amendments within about a year, and warned frequent changes worry investors.
Said the trust fund committee has broad discretion over funds and councils should be able to develop land under their own authority.

decisions: The Speaker did not accept the urgent question from the Keyodhoo member because it did not meet Rule 197 conditions.
First reading of the bill to amend the Tourism Act (Law 99/2) was announced.
Preliminary debate on the bill started; the Speaker did not accept several points of order as valid.
The Speaker decided to let all members who wished to speak do so before a vote and adjourned the sitting; next sitting set for Wednesday 12 March 2025 at 10:30.
